verse1.philosophical_explanation: Bhagavad Gita Chapter 15 Verse 1 offers a layered teaching on disciplined action, inner clarity, and God-centered wisdom, presenting dharma as a harmonizing principle that integrates duty, knowledge, devotion, and self-mastery. Ethical life in Sanatana Dharma emerges through disciplined action offered without egoic possessiveness, where one performs svadharma with humility and accountability. This teaching is socially relevant because it links personal transformation with collective order: families, communities, and governance remain stable only when conduct is rooted in justice, gratitude, and reverence for truth. Spiritually, the section invites bhakti and contemplative awareness, showing that liberation-oriented living can begin within ordinary duties when the heart is purified through right understanding and service.

verse.translation: 15.1 The Blessed Lord said They (the wise) speak of the indestructible peepul tree having its root above and branches below, whose leaves are the metres or hymns: he who knows it is a knower of the Vedas.

verse.transliteration: gāmāviśya ca bhūtāni dhārayāmyahamojasā . puṣṇāmi cauṣadhīḥ sarvāḥ somo bhūtvā rasātmakaḥ ||15-13||

verse.translation: 15.15 And I am seated in the hearts of all; from Me are memory and knowledge, as well as their absence. I am verily That which has to be known by all the Vedas; I am indeed the author of the Vedanta and the knower of the Vedas am I.
verse.transliteration: sarvasya cāhaṃ hṛdi sanniviṣṭo mattaḥ smṛtirjñānamapohanañca . vedaiśca sarvairahameva vedyo vedāntakṛdvedavideva cāham ||15-15||

verse5.philosophical_explanation: Bhagavad Gita Chapter 15 Verse 5 offers a layered teaching on disciplined action, inner clarity, and God-centered wisdom, presenting dharma as a harmonizing principle that integrates duty, knowledge, devotion, and self-mastery. In Vedantic reflection, the outer event is never merely external; it mirrors the inner field of the seeker where attachment, fear, pride, compassion, and discernment contend for dominance. The text therefore asks the reader to cultivate viveka, sustained discrimination between the permanent and the impermanent, while remaining active in righteous responsibilities. It also emphasizes that true strength is not aggression but alignment with satya, ahimsa in intent, self-restraint, and surrender to the Divine will. Ethical life in Sanatana Dharma emerges through disciplined action offered without egoic possessiveness, where one performs svadharma with humility and accountability. This teaching is socially relevant because it links personal transformation with collective order: families, communities, and governance remain stable only when conduct is rooted in justice, gratitude, and reverence for truth. Spiritually, the section invites bhakti and contemplative awareness, showing that liberation-oriented living can begin within ordinary duties when the heart is purified through right understanding and service.
verse5.scripture_text: निर्मानमोहा जितसङ्गदोषा अध्यात्मनित्या विनिवृत्तकामाः | द्वन्द्वैर्विमुक्ताः सुखदुःखसंज्ञैर्- गच्छन्त्यमूढाः पदमव्ययं तत् ||१५-५||

verse.sanskrit: निर्मानमोहा जितसङ्गदोषा अध्यात्मनित्या विनिवृत्तकामाः | द्वन्द्वैर्विमुक्ताः सुखदुःखसंज्ञैर्- गच्छन्त्यमूढाः पदमव्ययं तत् ||१५-५||
verse.translation: 15.5 Free from pride and delusion, victorious over the evil of attachment, dwelling constantly in the Self, their desires having completely turned away, freed from the pairs of opposites known as pleasure and pain, the undeluded reach the eternal goal.
verse.transliteration: nirmānamohā jitasaṅgadoṣā adhyātmanityā vinivṛttakāmāḥ . dvandvairvimuktāḥ sukhaduḥkhasaṃjñaira- gacchantyamūḍhāḥ padamavyayaṃ tat ||15-5||

verse.translation: 15.7 An eternal portion of Myself having become a living soul in the world of life, draws to (itself) the (five) senses with the mind for the sixth, abiding in Nature.
verse.transliteration: mamaivāṃśo jīvaloke jīvabhūtaḥ sanātanaḥ . manaḥṣaṣṭhānīndriyāṇi prakṛtisthāni karṣati ||15-7||
